seo.title: Prepare for Shabbat
seo.description: Prepare for your first Shabbat visit to Temple Aviv Judea in Fullerton. Find service times, what to expect, family information, meal guidance, and ways to connect.

hero.title: Come curious. You are welcome.
hero.intro: Whether Messianic Jewish worship is familiar or completely new, here is what to expect so you and your family can arrive at ease.

banner.imageAlt: Mosaic artwork of a worshipper sounding the shofar over Jerusalem

welcomeCard.heading: Who will I meet?
welcomeCard.body: Our mishpachah is a diverse community of Jewish and Gentile believers from many ethnicities and faith backgrounds. What draws us together is love—for G-d, for one another, and for every person who walks through the door.

service.heading: Ancient patterns, wholehearted praise.
service.body: Our Shabbat gathering weaves together traditional Jewish liturgy, musical worship, singing, and Davidic dance. We bless our children, hear a message from Scripture through a Jewish perspective, and close with the Aaronic Blessing.
service.flowIntro: The readings and message change each week, while the recurring rhythm includes:
flow: Readings from the Torah, Haftarah, and Brit Chadasha
Blessings over bread, wine, and the children

questions.heading: What should I wear?
questions.body: Come presentable, modest, and comfortable. You do not need special clothing or prior knowledge of Jewish tradition to participate.

questions.heading: What about children?
questions.body: Children are part of our community. We offer Shabbat School during the morning and have a crying room available for families with little ones.

questions.heading: Can I stay for lunch?
questions.body: Absolutely. Everyone is invited to stay for our weekly Oneg meal. If you choose to bring food, please do not bring pork or shellfish.

questions.heading: What happens after the service?
questions.body: Stay for Oneg and conversation, then join Rabbi’s Corner to explore the weekly Torah portion and ask questions. Community life also includes a monthly women’s gathering, Davidic dance instruction, and opportunities to serve one another and our neighbors.

personalWelcome.heading: Let us welcome you personally.
personalWelcome.body: Rabbi Corey would be glad to meet you over lunch or by appointment and answer your questions. First-time visitors may also receive a hospitality package. Call and leave a message, or send an email, and we will help you feel prepared.

location.body: Just a few blocks from downtown Fullerton on Commonwealth Avenue.
